senses.sense_definition: An early symptom or warning sign indicating the onset of a disease or illness.

examples.text: Fatigue and sensitivity to light often serve as a <w>prodrome</w> before a severe migraine begins.
The doctor explained that mild confusion can be a critical <w>prodrome</w> of the neurological condition.

senses.sense_definition: A precursor, harbinger, or early warning event of something to come.

examples.text: Many historians viewed the widespread protests as a dangerous <w>prodrome</w> to civil conflict.
The minor diplomatic dispute proved to be a dark <w>prodrome</w> of the impending war.

senses.sense_definition: An introductory publication, preliminary book, or treatise that precedes a fuller work.

examples.text: The scientist published a brief <w>prodrome</w> outlining his theories before writing the complete book.
Her academic <w>prodrome</w> offered readers a valuable glimpse into the findings of her forthcoming study.

traits.comment: Used historically in academic or scientific writing.

senses.sense_definition: Serving as an early warning sign; <w>prodromous</w>.

examples.text: The physician monitored the patient for any <w>prodrome</w> indications of a viral infection.
A sudden loss of appetite was recorded as a <w>prodrome</w> condition before the fever developed.

traits.comment: Rarely used adjectivally; prodromal is more standard.
